climate.koppen_name: Cold, no dry season, hot summer

climate: Seasons this mild ripen Merlot, Riesling, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Cabernet Sauvignon is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.

soil.rock: Gravel drains fast and is poor, so roots go deep for water and food. It holds little water. Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.
